description_full: Bentley Systems, Incorporated, together with its subsidiaries, provides infrastructure engineering software solutions in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia-Pacific. The company offers open modeling applications, such as MicroStation, OpenBridge, OpenBuildings, OpenFlows, OpenPlant, OpenRail, OpenRoads, OpenSite and OpenSite+, OpenTower, OpenTunnel, and OpenUtilities; and open simulation applications, including ADINA, AutoPIPE, LEGION, OpenPaths, Power Line Systems, RAM, SACS, SPIDA, and STAAD; and geoprofessional applications for modeling and simulation of near and deep subsurface conditions, including AGS, Central, GeoStudio, Imago, Leapfrog, MX Deposit, Oasis montaj, OpenGround, and PLAXIS. It also provides infrastructure cloud applications, such as ProjectWise, SYNCHRO, and AssetWise, as well as Cesium and iTwin platform that enables users to create and curate cloud native digital representations of physical infrastructure assets consisting of iTwin Capture, iTwin Engage, iTwin Experience, and iTwin IoT platforms. The company serves civil, structural, geotechnical, subsurface, process engineers, architects, geospatial professionals, city and regional planners, contractors, fabricators, and operations and maintenance engineers. Bentley Systems, Incorporated was incorporated in 1984 and is headquartered in Exton, Pennsylvania.
ceo_bio: Mr. Nicholas H. Cumins | CEO & Director | Age 48 | Compensation: $1.7M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 5K people. Revenue per employee of $259K ranks in the below the sector median among Technology peers, improving at 13%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $90K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $13K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 7× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (7/10).
financial_summary: Bentley Systems, Incorporated is a large-cap technology business with a $13.5B market cap on $1.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 79% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $520M in free cash flow — roughly 35 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.94× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 48× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 45% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 24% operating margin runs 17pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.03x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+2.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 22% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 27% over the last three months.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 7% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 42% and a beta of 1.05, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.09 vs 5y 1.07), so read it loosely.
About $78.8M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 14% in the 2020 crash and 43% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $37.77 (margin of safety -18%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 30%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $24.80 to $58.41 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 44.2 vs 26.7 and EV/EBITDA 31.3 vs 16.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 35% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.9% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 15 covering analysts target $44.67 on average, in line with the price.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 9.5%, but the 0pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.47).
It runs a 79% gross margin and converts 35% of revenue into free cash flow, or 30% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.94x.
ROE of 23% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (3.0x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 5pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 20.5% of revenue on R&D and 4.8% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.1x net debt to EBITDA ($123.3M of cash against $1.2B of debt), with interest covered 47.8x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.0, in the safe zone).
The current ratio of 0.56 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 70% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.0% over 3 years and 13.4% over 5 years, so growth is decelerating.
Free cash flow has compounded 16.5% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.02, a backlog worth 20% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 13%.
Capex runs only 0.3x depreciation (1.2% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 43, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 45.3%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 56%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.6% (0.9% in buybacks and 0.6% in dividends).
The share count has grown 1.7% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 5,800 employees, each generates about $259K of revenue, 0.7x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 13.4% a year.
That works out to $90K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.7M (7x revenue per employee).
